_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices badge (passing level): Lodger's answers, read by bestpractices.dev. Update this file when a change affects an answer.
description_good_justification: The README says in its first lines what Lodger does and for whom: a web UI for the KVM/QEMU VMs on an existing Linux host, without a reinstall. It also lists what Lodger does today and what it does not do. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README explains how to install Lodger, how to report a vulnerability, and where the contributor docs are. Bugs and ideas go to GitHub issues, with issue templates. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the process: a pull request to main with a Conventional Commits title, a changeset for a user-facing change, and the checks to run. It also says that Lodger accepts no pull requests yet, until most planned features exist. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the rules that each change must follow, such as tests that can fail, no subprocess calls, and no secret in a log, and the checks that must pass. The pull request template repeats them. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: The license is in the LICENSE file at the repository root. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README and the documentation site cover installation, upgrades, reverse proxies, AppArmor, and security. https://schubydoo.github.io/lodger/
documentation_interface_justification: The documentation site covers the command line (install, uninstall, doctor, and the root recovery commands) and the configuration keys for network access. The installed /etc/lodger/config.toml explains every key in its comments, and `lodger --help` documents each command. The HTTP API serves only Lodger's own web app, so it has no public reference. https://schubydoo.github.io/lodger/
sites_https_justification: The repository and the documentation site use HTTPS only. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger and https://schubydoo.github.io/lodger/
discussion_justification: GitHub issues are searchable, each has a URL, and anyone with a GitHub account can take part. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/issues
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, and issues are in English.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public Git repository. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when.
repo_interim_justification: Every change goes through a pull request to main, so interim versions are public.
repo_distributed_justification: The repository uses Git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version, starting with v0.1.0. Knope computes the next version from the changeset fragments. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/releases
version_semver_justification: Releases use Semantic Versioning, starting with 0.1.0. Until 1.0, any release can break the configuration, the API, or the stored data, and the README says so.
version_tags_justification: Each release has a v<version> tag, such as v0.1.0, and a ruleset protects the v* tags. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/tags
release_notes_justification: Each release has notes in CHANGELOG.md and on its GitHub release. Knope writes them from the one-line changeset fragment that each user-facing change adds. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability yet. The release notes name each such fix, with its CVE if one exists.
report_process_justification: Bug reports go to GitHub issues, with issue templates. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/issues
report_responses_justification: No bug report came in during the last 2-12 months, so the project acknowledged every report in that period.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request came in during the last 2-12 months, so the project responded to every request in that period.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues keep a public, searchable archive of reports and responses. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md explains how to report a vulnerability through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, what to include, and what to expect. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled for the repository. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report came in during the last 6 months. SECURITY.md promises an answer within a few days.
build_justification: Cargo builds the Rust workspace, pnpm builds the SvelteKit web UI, and `just build` runs both.
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses Cargo, pnpm, and just.
build_floss_tools_justification: Every build tool is free software: Rust, Cargo, Node.js, pnpm, and just.
test_justification: The Rust tests run with cargo-nextest, the web tests with Vitest, and the browser flows with Playwright and axe. All run in CI.
test_invocation_justification: `just check` runs fmt, clippy, and the Rust tests, and `pnpm run test` in web/ runs the web tests. AGENTS.md documents both.
test_most_justification: CI fails when Rust line coverage drops below 90% (cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 90).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs every test on each pull request and on each push to main.
test_policy_justification: AGENTS.md requires tests for each change, and each new test must be shown to fail when the code breaks. The pull request template asks for them.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature pull requests add tests with the change.
tests_documented_added_justification: AGENTS.md and the pull request template state the test policy.
warnings_justification: CI runs clippy and rustdoc with -D warnings, eslint, prettier, and svelte-check.
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings fail CI, so each one is fixed before a merge.
warnings_strict_justification: Every clippy warning is an error (-D warnings), plus the workspace lint configuration.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designs against OWASP ASVS 5.0. The threat model and the ASVS Level 1 checklist, which Lodger passes with no open item, are in the repository. The controls include __Host- session cookies, CSRF tokens, an Origin check, a Content Security Policy, and a hardened systemd unit. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
know_common_errors_justification: The review rules in .github/claude-review-instructions.md check for common errors: injection through string-built XML or YAML, subprocess calls, secrets in logs, and endpoints without a session.
crypto_published_justification: Lodger uses only published algorithms: argon2id for passwords, SHA-256 for hashes, ECDSA P-256 for its self-signed certificates, and the TLS 1.2 and 1.3 cipher suites of rustls.
crypto_call_justification: Lodger calls the RustCrypto argon2 and sha2 crates, getrandom, rustls with the ring provider, and rcgen. It implements no cryptography itself.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic libraries are free software: RustCrypto, getrandom, rustls, ring, and rcgen.
crypto_keylength_justification: `lodger install --self-signed` makes an ECDSA P-256 key, which gives 128 bits of security, above the NIST minimum of 112 bits.
crypto_working_justification: Lodger uses no broken algorithm (no MD5, SHA-1, or DES) for a security purpose.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Lodger uses no algorithm or mode with a known serious weakness.
crypto_pfs_justification: Built-in TLS uses rustls, which allows only ECDHE key exchange in TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3, so every connection has perfect forward secrecy. Behind a reverse proxy, the proxy negotiates TLS.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Passwords are stored as argon2id hashes with a random salt, with parameters at the OWASP minimum.
crypto_random_justification: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, setup tokens, and WebSocket tickets come from getrandom, the operating system's secure random source.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases download over HTTPS from GitHub. Each release has SHA-256 checksums, a cosign signature of checksums.txt, and SLSA build provenance, and install.sh checks the checksum and, with cosign, the signature before it installs anything.
delivery_unsigned_justification: checksums.txt carries a keyless cosign signature from the release workflow, and install.sh refuses a bad or missing signature when cosign is installed. The installation page shows how to check it by hand. https://github.com/schubydoo/lodger/blob/main/docs/installation.md
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability is open. CI runs cargo audit, cargo deny, and pnpm audit, and Renovate updates dependencies.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No valid credential is in the repository. gitleaks scans the new commits of each pull request and push, and the full history every week. Its allowlist holds only one fake token from a test.
static_analysis_justification: CI runs clippy with -D warnings, CodeQL for Rust and TypeScript, zizmor for the workflows, cargo audit, cargo deny, and OpenSSF Scorecard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL looks for common vulnerability classes in the Rust and TypeScript code, and zizmor looks for common workflow misconfigurations.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Medium and higher findings are fixed before a merge. The main ruleset blocks a merge on a high CodeQL alert.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and push, and CodeQL and Scorecard also run weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A nightly job runs stress tests of the two FFI modules under AddressSanitizer and LeakSanitizer. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzes the XML parsers, the XML builders, and the input checks of lodger-core on each pull request that changes them and every 2 days, and it found and fixed a real bug on its first run.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The only unsafe code is in two FFI modules, and a nightly job runs their stress tests under AddressSanitizer and LeakSanitizer. A CI guard rejects unsafe code anywhere else.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The sanitizer tests run as a test build, so debug assertions are on.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No defect found by dynamic analysis is open.
